mbm-1501.clue: The bunker rake lives upside down in my bag.
mbm-1501.quote: I raked the sand smooth after my shot and found three heron tracks crossing it. I went around them. A bird that gets out of that trap in three deserves its score recorded.

mbm-1502.clue: I owe my little sister a very small bridge.
mbm-1502.quote: At the windmill hole my ball stopped halfway across the drawbridge. My sister charged me one gummy worm to lower it. She had brought the exact change she wanted.

mbm-1503.clue: I've got a shiny patch on each sock.
mbm-1503.quote: Our first lesson took place in stocking feet on Aunt May's linoleum. I forgot every step at the ballroom except the little slide where her kitchen table used to be.

mbm-1504.clue: I fold the map around something that rattles.
mbm-1504.quote: At the summit my dad opened his lunch tin. He'd carried the chipped blue teacup all the way up because my mother always said tea tasted better with a view.

mbm-1505.clue: I found a matching pair of sunsets.
mbm-1505.quote: We coasted home after the last run with my red skis sticking straight up in the boat. Each glossy tip caught a whole pink sky. I made the driver wait while I got a picture.

mbm-1506.clue: I can tell how heavy yesterday was by the color of the ribbon.
mbm-1506.quote: My first pair of dumbbells belonged to my aunt. She tied a blue ribbon to the lighter one when she started again after a long break. I tied one to mine the day we lifted together.

mbm-1507.clue: I've got an audience on the clothesline.
mbm-1507.quote: I took a tricky high note out onto the balcony. The neighbor's canary answered from behind a sheet. We traded it back and forth until the laundry stopped moving.

mbm-1508.clue: I can still find the kitchen with the lights out.
mbm-1508.quote: When our old house came down, I pieced the floor plan into a quilt. Grandma traced her way from the front door to the stove and asked why I hadn't put the kettle on.

mbm-1509.clue: My timetable has a pressed leaf between two departures.
mbm-1509.quote: Every autumn I wait at the footbridge for the yellow caboose to pass the red maple. This year the last leaf came down with it. I caught it in my open timetable.

mbm-1510.clue: My training partner counts the pauses, too.
mbm-1510.quote: We took a dented kitchen timer to the rec center because I always rushed my rests. When the bell rang, a man two benches over asked whether the cookies were done.

mbm-1511.clue: I save one space in the dry bag for music.
mbm-1511.quote: At the quiet bend I blew across my empty drink bottle. Our guide answered from the stern with a lower note. We floated past three fishermen sounding like a very small tugboat.

mbm-1512.clue: I've got a seam that goes straight through a rainbow.
mbm-1512.quote: My nephew chose scraps by lining them up against his box of crayons. We ran out of violet, so he donated the pocket from his favorite pajama shirt. He checks on it when he visits.

mbm-1513.clue: I have a picture of our boat taken from underneath.
mbm-1513.quote: We stopped above a deep green pool and could see our red raft upside down in the water. I leaned out to photograph it. You can just make out my helmet hanging from the bottom of the sky.

mbm-1514.clue: Count the little dents on the handle.
mbm-1514.quote: My grandpa's carrying case always slipped when his hands got wet. I wrapped the handle in leather and stamped in four shallow finger grooves. It fits exactly one grandpa.

mbm-1515.clue: I saved the tiniest triangle for the porch.
mbm-1515.quote: I made our neighborhood in scraps of cloth. The yellow porch light on Mrs. Lee's house is smaller than my thumbnail. She spotted it from across the room.

mbm-1516.clue: I've never paddled so hard to stay in one place.
mbm-1516.quote: A pelican perched on the channel marker while I sketched it from my kayak. Every time I put my pencil down to paddle back, it changed legs.

mbm-1517.clue: You can see whose hand was smaller.
mbm-1517.quote: I threw a mixing bowl, then my little cousin pressed one thumb into its foot. When I turn it upside down to dry, there we both are, her print tucked inside mine.

mbm-1518.clue: I packed my good socks for the dock.
mbm-1518.quote: My first clean crossing earned me a dry pair of socks and a spot on the pier rail to hang the wet ones. The other skiers had lined theirs up by color. Mine finished the rainbow.

mbm-1519.clue: My running map looks like a breakfast order.
mbm-1519.quote: My niece drew a route shaped like a fried egg. I followed her crooked pencil line for three miles. The yolk was a park bench where she'd left me an orange.

mbm-1520.clue: I keep a little bell under the game board.
mbm-1520.quote: Mum won't interrupt a good strategy even when dinner's ready. Now she rings the hotel bell and auctions off the first dumpling. I have lost entire kingdoms for less.

mbm-1521.clue: I put an extra beat in the song for the door.
mbm-1521.quote: The rehearsal-room door squeaked in the same key as our chorus. We timed the break so the drummer could swing it open. That's the loudest cheer we've ever had for a hinge.

mbm-1522.clue: My chalk bag has a daisy on the bottom.
mbm-1522.quote: I stitched it there so my belayer would have something nice to look at while I thought about the next move. She says that flower's had some very long afternoons.

mbm-1523.clue: I stand where the little crab tells me to.
mbm-1523.quote: On our court a crab kept digging in the corner where nobody served. We gave it that square for the afternoon. My partner says it's the best line judge we've had.

mbm-1524.clue: I know how much breakfast weighs to a duck.
mbm-1524.quote: My uncle brought toast in a tin for our dawn paddle. One duck followed the canoe all the way to the landing, then waddled past us to the café. Regular customer, apparently.

mbm-1525.clue: Look at the feet before you look at the wings.
mbm-1525.quote: I built a little courier robot and painted mud on its boots. My brother asked what happened to its rocket pack. Nothing. Some parcels deserve to be walked to the door.
